notice: Educational summaries for Tanzania. Conditions and recommendations vary by agro-ecological zone, variety, season, soil test, and local veterinary or extension advice. This catalog is not a diagnosis, pesticide label, ration formulation, or substitute for official instructions.

sources.name: Tanzania Agricultural Research Institute (TARI)
sources.scope: Crop research, crop varieties, production practices, and agricultural publications.

sources.name: Tanzania Plant Health and Pesticides Authority (TPHPA)
sources.scope: Plant health, pest surveillance, and pesticide registration and safety.

sources.name: Ministry of Livestock and Fisheries, Tanzania
sources.scope: Livestock services, animal health, feed resources, and government publications.

sources.name: Tanzania Meteorological Authority (TMA)
sources.scope: Official weather warnings, forecasts, and seasonal and agricultural forecasts.

sources.name: Tanzania Forest Services Agency (TFS)
sources.scope: Forestry and beekeeping services and official publications.

crops.name: Maize
crops.summary: A major grain and food crop grown across Tanzania. Suitable variety, planting window, and practices depend on altitude, rainfall pattern, and local recommendations.

guide.siteSelection: Choose a site with adequate drainage and a locally recommended variety. Use a soil test and local seasonal forecast; avoid assuming a single calendar applies to every district.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare a level, weed-managed seedbed while protecting soil structure. In erosion-prone areas, use contour-aligned rows and retain suitable residues.
guide.planting: Plant into moist soil after locally reliable onset of rains. Use certified seed of a variety recommended for the zone; follow the seed supplier or extension officer for spacing, seed rate, and plant population.
guide.nutrition: Base fertilizer and lime decisions on a soil test and crop recommendations. Place fertilizer safely away from seed; split applications only as directed by locally validated guidance.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Keep the crop weed-free during early establishment. Monitor moisture at establishment, flowering, and grain filling; protect drainage and avoid unnecessary water stress.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout seedlings and whorls for fall armyworm, stalk borers, and unusual damage. Check for maize lethal necrosis, leaf diseases, and storage pests. Confirm uncertain symptoms before acting.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest at physiological maturity and dry grain safely to a storage-appropriate moisture level. Keep grain off bare ground; clean stores and protect grain from moisture, insects, rodents, and contamination.
guide.records: Record seed variety and lot, planting date, field and GPS, rainfall observations, inputs, scouting, harvest quantity, and storage losses.

crops.name: Rice
crops.summary: A cereal grown in irrigated and rain-fed systems. Water control, seed quality, and locally suitable varieties are central to production.

guide.siteSelection: Choose a site and production system suited to available water, soil, drainage, and the local rice market. Confirm whether the variety is adapted to irrigated or rain-fed conditions.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare a level field and functional bunds where the chosen system uses standing water. Maintain inlets and drainage so excess water can be managed.
guide.planting: Use clean, recommended seed. Direct seeding and transplanting need different timing and management; follow local extension advice for seed rate, nursery, spacing, and transplant age.
guide.nutrition: Use soil-test results and locally recommended rice guidance. Avoid nutrient applications immediately before water discharge; keep records of products and dates.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Manage water depth and drainage according to crop stage and system. Early weed control is important; use approved cultural methods and obtain local advice before herbicide use.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for stem borers, planthoppers, blast-like lesions, and bacterial symptoms. Avoid overusing nitrogen and protect beneficial organisms; confirm diagnosis before treatment.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest when most grains reach the locally recommended maturity. Dry on a clean surface, thresh carefully, and store dry grain in a clean, pest-managed structure.
guide.records: Record water source and schedule, seed, nursery or direct-seeding method, input use, pest observations, harvest date, and grain quality.

crops.name: Wheat
crops.summary: A cool-season cereal most suitable to locally adapted highland conditions. Variety choice and disease management require zone-specific advice.

guide.siteSelection: Select a well-drained field and a variety recommended for the elevation and local season. Check local rainfall and temperature outlooks before planting.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare a fine, even seedbed without working saturated soil. Use erosion-conscious practices on slopes.
guide.planting: Use clean, certified seed and follow the local recommendation for sowing window, row spacing, and seed rate. Avoid carrying seed-borne problems into a new season.
guide.nutrition: Use soil analysis and local recommendations for nutrient type and timing. Do not copy fertilizer rates from another region or crop.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Maintain early weed control and monitor moisture through establishment and grain filling. Protect the field from waterlogging.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for rusts, blotches, aphids, and lodging risk. Seek local diagnosis when disease appears; use resistant varieties where officially recommended.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest at suitable grain maturity, dry thoroughly, and store in a clean, dry, ventilated and pest-managed place.
guide.records: Track variety, source, sowing and harvest dates, field conditions, disease observations, input decisions, and grain quality.

crops.name: Sorghum
crops.summary: A drought-tolerant cereal used for food, feed, and processing. Local variety, bird pressure, and grain use influence management.

guide.siteSelection: Choose a locally recommended variety for rainfall pattern, maturity, grain or forage use, and bird pressure. Drought tolerance does not mean the crop needs no water.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare a firm, weed-managed seedbed and use soil and water conservation where runoff is likely.
guide.planting: Sow after effective rainfall onset using clean seed and local guidance for spacing and seed rate. Keep a uniform stand and avoid late planting without extension advice.
guide.nutrition: Base nutrient inputs on soil condition, intended use, and local recommendations. Rotate or intercrop where locally suitable.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Control weeds early and conserve soil moisture with suitable residue or water-harvesting practices.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for shoot fly, stem borers, grain mold, and head-feeding pests. Monitor birds around grain maturity and use locally approved non-harmful deterrence.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest at maturity and dry heads or grain thoroughly. Protect stored grain from moisture and insects.
guide.records: Record variety, planting date, rainfall, bird and pest pressure, grain or forage use, yield, and storage condition.

crops.name: Pearl Millet
crops.summary: A resilient small-grain cereal used for food and feed. Choose locally adapted seed for rainfall pattern, maturity, and intended use.

guide.siteSelection: Select a locally recommended variety for rainfall pattern, maturity, soil, and grain or forage use.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare a weed-managed seedbed and conserve soil moisture; avoid unnecessary deep tillage on fragile soils.
guide.planting: Plant clean seed after effective rainfall and follow local guidance for seed rate, spacing, and thinning.
guide.nutrition: Use soil-test results and locally validated recommendations; rotate with suitable legumes where practical.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Control weeds early, protect establishment moisture, and monitor for erosion and prolonged dry spells.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for shoot fly, head-feeding pests, birds, and grain mold. Confirm the cause before using any crop-protection product.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest mature heads, dry thoroughly, thresh cleanly, and keep grain protected from moisture, rodents, and insects.
guide.records: Record variety, seed source, planting conditions, bird pressure, harvest use, and storage losses.

crops.name: Finger Millet
crops.summary: A small-grain cereal grown for food and other uses. Establishment, seed handling, and maturity vary by local variety.

guide.siteSelection: Select a locally adapted variety and a field with suitable drainage and rainfall for the chosen production system.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare a clean, fine seedbed and protect soil structure and moisture, especially on slopes.
guide.planting: Use clean seed and local advice on direct sowing or transplanting, seed rate, spacing, and thinning.
guide.nutrition: Base soil amendments and fertilizer on a soil test and local extension recommendations.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Manage weeds during establishment and protect the crop from waterlogging or prolonged moisture stress.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for blast-like leaf or head symptoms, shoot pests, birds, and storage insects; seek confirmation before control.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest mature heads, dry them thoroughly, thresh cleanly, and store grain in a dry, pest-managed place.
guide.records: Record variety, establishment method, seed source, disease observations, harvest, and storage condition.

crops.name: Barley
crops.summary: A cool-season cereal and feed or malting crop. Variety, quality standards, and suitability depend on location and buyer requirements.

guide.siteSelection: Confirm local suitability, variety, and market specification before planting; use a well-drained field.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare a uniform seedbed and use erosion control on sloping land.
guide.planting: Use quality seed and follow local recommendations for planting window, seed rate, and row spacing.
guide.nutrition: Use soil-test results and crop-specific local nutrient guidance; avoid applying an uncalibrated rate.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Control weeds early and monitor moisture through establishment and grain filling while preventing waterlogging.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for rusts, smuts, foliar diseases, aphids, and lodging; seek local diagnosis and seed-health advice.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest at suitable grain maturity, dry safely, and store according to the buyer's quality and moisture requirements.
guide.records: Track variety, seed lot, crop protection, harvest moisture, quality testing, and buyer requirements.

crops.name: Oats
crops.summary: A cereal grown for grain, forage, or both. Local climate and end use determine the suitable variety and harvest stage.

guide.siteSelection: Choose a locally suitable variety and decide whether the crop is for grain, forage, or dual use.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare a firm, weed-managed seedbed with drainage suited to local rainfall.
guide.planting: Use clean seed and regional recommendations for sowing time, seed rate, and row spacing.
guide.nutrition: Use soil tests and local cereal or forage recommendations for nutrient decisions.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Manage weeds early and monitor moisture; maintain drainage in wet conditions.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for rusts, leaf blotches, aphids, and lodging; use locally advised resistant varieties and practices.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Choose harvest stage for grain or forage purpose. Dry and store grain safely; conserve forage hygienically.
guide.records: Record variety, seed source, intended use, harvest stage, yield, and storage or forage quality.

crops.name: Common beans
crops.summary: A food legume that contributes dietary protein and can support crop rotation. Variety and disease pressure vary by zone.

guide.siteSelection: Use a locally adapted variety and a well-drained field. Avoid repeating beans continuously where soil-borne disease is a concern.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare a weed-managed seedbed while preserving soil structure. Use clean seed from a reliable source.
guide.planting: Plant into moist soil in the locally recommended window. Follow local instructions for spacing, seed rate, and seed treatment.
guide.nutrition: Use soil-test guidance; beans need appropriate phosphorus and other nutrients but fertilizer must be locally calibrated. Avoid assuming inoculants or nutrient products will suit every site.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Manage weeds early and avoid waterlogging. Protect flowering and pod development from severe moisture stress where possible.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for bean fly, aphids, angular leaf spot, anthracnose, and rust-like pustules. Rotate crops, use clean seed, and confirm symptoms with extension support.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest when pods mature, dry carefully, and store clean grain dry in a sealed, pest-managed container.
guide.records: Record variety, seed source, planting date, disease and pest signs, harvest quality, and storage treatments.

crops.name: Tomato
crops.summary: A high-value vegetable grown in open fields and protected systems. It needs careful water, sanitation, and pest monitoring.

guide.siteSelection: Select a site with good drainage, reliable water, and a rotation history that reduces solanaceous disease pressure. Choose varieties for local market and disease constraints.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare raised beds or drainage channels where needed. Clean tools and use healthy seedlings from a trusted source.
guide.planting: Harden seedlings before transplanting and follow local variety guidance for spacing and support. Avoid transplanting stressed or diseased seedlings.
guide.nutrition: Use a soil test and crop-stage recommendations. Split nutrient applications when locally advised; avoid fertilizer contact with stems and roots.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Irrigate consistently without wetting foliage where feasible. Mulch and manage weeds to reduce soil splash and competition.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout leaf undersides and fruit for tomato leafminer, whiteflies, aphids, late blight, bacterial wilt, and virus symptoms. Remove suspect plants safely and seek confirmation.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest at the stage required by the market, handle gently, sort damaged fruit, and keep produce cool and shaded.
guide.records: Record seedling source, transplant date, irrigation, scouting, crop-protection product and label details, harvest grade, and losses.

crops.name: Potato
crops.summary: A cool-season tuber crop requiring healthy seed tubers, good drainage, and close monitoring for late blight and bacterial diseases.

guide.siteSelection: Use a well-drained field with a rotation history that reduces potato and tomato disease carry-over. Plant clean, locally recommended seed tubers.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare loose soil and workable ridges; avoid planting into waterlogged ground.
guide.planting: Use inspected or otherwise trusted seed tubers and follow local guidance for seed size, spacing, and planting date. Earth up as advised to protect tubers from light.
guide.nutrition: Base fertilizer on soil analysis and local potato recommendations; avoid applying uncalibrated rates.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Maintain even soil moisture without prolonged saturation. Keep weeds managed and drainage functional.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout frequently for late blight, bacterial wilt, viruses, and tuber moth. Isolate suspect seed lots and seek extension diagnosis before chemical decisions.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest after skin set where applicable, avoid bruising, cure and sort tubers, and store dark, ventilated, and protected from pests.
guide.records: Record seed lot, field rotation, disease scouting, ridge management, harvest grade, and storage losses.

crops.name: Banana
crops.summary: A perennial food and cash crop. Planting material health, soil moisture, mat management, and disease sanitation are important.

guide.siteSelection: Choose a site with suitable rainfall or irrigation, drainage, and wind protection. Use disease-free planting material recommended for the area.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare planting stations and conserve organic matter. Avoid planting where water remains stagnant.
guide.planting: Use clean suckers or approved planting material and locally advised spacing. Keep varieties and planting dates documented.
guide.nutrition: Maintain soil organic matter and follow local recommendations based on soil tests and expected harvest. Avoid fertilizer contact with plant tissue.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Keep young mats free from weed competition, mulch where suitable, and maintain drainage. Remove excess suckers according to local production guidance.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Inspect planting material and mats for wilt, leaf streaking, bunchy top-like symptoms, weevils, and nematode damage. Remove and dispose of infected material as advised.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest bunches at market maturity, protect from bruising, and use clean handling and shade after harvest.
guide.records: Track planting material source, mat age, sucker management, disease observations, bunch harvest, and market grade.

crops.name: Coffee
crops.summary: A perennial cash crop with distinct Arabica and Robusta needs. Select species and variety for the local elevation, climate, and market.

guide.siteSelection: Confirm species and variety suitability with the local coffee extension service. Protect soil and water on slopes and maintain appropriate shade where recommended.
guide.landPreparation: Establish drainage and erosion control before planting. Use healthy seedlings from a known source.
guide.planting: Follow local guidance for planting season, spacing, shade, pruning system, and replacement of missing trees.
guide.nutrition: Use soil tests and coffee-specific local recommendations; account for tree age and expected yield. Do not apply generic rates.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Maintain suitable ground cover, control competing weeds, and monitor drought stress and drainage.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for coffee berry disease, leaf rust, berry borers, and stem pests. Confirm disease and coordinate management with local extension and current official guidance.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest ripe cherries as required by the processing method. Keep lots clean and process or dry promptly to protect cup quality.
guide.records: Record species, variety, tree age, pruning, flowering, disease observations, harvest lot, processing, and buyer quality feedback.

crops.name: Tea
crops.summary: A perennial leaf crop suited to particular cool, wet highland environments. Harvest and pruning cycles are location- and factory-specific.

guide.siteSelection: Confirm altitude, rainfall, soil acidity, and factory access suitability with local tea extension services before establishing a field.
guide.landPreparation: Protect slopes with contour practices and drainage. Establish wind protection and ground cover where recommended.
guide.planting: Use recommended clones and healthy planting material. Follow local advice on spacing, planting season, formative pruning, and plucking table establishment.
guide.nutrition: Use soil and leaf analysis where available and follow locally approved tea recommendations. Keep nutrient and lime decisions specific to tea.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Manage weeds without exposing soil on slopes. Maintain drainage and conserve moisture during dry periods.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout regularly for leaf and stem pests and fungal diseases. Consult a tea extension officer before selecting control measures.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Pluck the locally specified tender shoot standard and deliver fresh leaf promptly in clean, ventilated collection containers.
guide.records: Record clone, field age, pruning cycle, plucking dates, green-leaf weight, quality feedback, and inputs.

crops.name: Groundnuts
crops.summary: A food and oilseed legume. Clean seed, rotation, timely harvest, and careful drying help manage aflatoxin risk.

guide.siteSelection: Choose well-drained soil and a variety suited to local rainfall and market. Avoid fields with recent groundnut disease history.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare a friable seedbed to support pegging and pod development. Maintain erosion control.
guide.planting: Use sound, clean seed and local guidance for shelling, seed rate, spacing, and planting window.
guide.nutrition: Follow soil-test advice; calcium availability near pod development may be important, but amendments should be locally recommended.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Control weeds early and avoid waterlogging. Maintain moisture during flowering, pegging, and pod fill where possible.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for leaf spots, rosette symptoms, termites, and soil pests. Remove infected plants as advised and rotate crops.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest at maturity, dry pods promptly on clean raised surfaces, sort damaged pods, and store dry in a moisture-protected place to reduce aflatoxin risk.
guide.records: Record seed source, rotation, disease signs, harvest date, drying duration, damaged pods, and storage conditions.

crops.name: Cashew
crops.summary: A perennial tree crop important in coastal and southern production areas. Orchard hygiene, tree age, and nut quality matter.

guide.siteSelection: Use a locally recommended variety and site. Consider tree spacing, drainage, wind exposure, and access for nut collection.
guide.landPreparation: Protect soil and water, mark planting stations, and establish young trees with careful weed management.
guide.planting: Use healthy planting material and local extension recommendations for planting, spacing, pruning, and replacement.
guide.nutrition: Use soil-test information and cashew-specific extension advice, particularly for orchard age and expected production.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Maintain young-tree moisture and keep basins weed-managed without damaging roots. Manage orchard ground cover and drainage.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout flowering and nut set for pests and fungal disease; remove and dispose of affected material as advised. Seek diagnosis before treatment.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Collect mature fallen nuts frequently, separate from spoiled material, dry safely, and store in clean, dry conditions.
guide.records: Track variety, tree age, pruning, flowering, pest observations, nut quantity, grade, drying, and storage.

crops.name: Cotton
crops.summary: A fibre crop with pest-sensitive flowering and boll stages. Follow local seasonal recommendations and integrated pest management.

guide.siteSelection: Choose an approved variety and field that fits local rainfall, rotation, and market requirements.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare a well-drained field and manage residues in line with local pest and disease recommendations.
guide.planting: Use quality seed and follow current regional advice on sowing window, spacing, and plant population.
guide.nutrition: Base nutrient decisions on soil tests and local cotton guidance. Avoid excessive vegetative growth from unbalanced inputs.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Control weeds early and monitor moisture through flowering and boll development. Avoid waterlogging.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for bollworms, sucking pests, and wilt symptoms at intervals recommended by local extension. Preserve beneficial insects and use only currently registered products according to their exact label.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Pick clean, dry open bolls and keep seed cotton free from soil, plastic, and moisture contamination.
guide.records: Record seed source, planting, scouting, beneficial insects, any labeled pesticide use, picking rounds, and contamination.

crops.name: Sunflower
crops.summary: An oilseed crop adapted to several semi-arid and sub-humid systems. Pollination, birds, and harvest timing affect yield and quality.

guide.siteSelection: Select a locally recommended variety with suitable maturity and market use. Choose a well-drained field with adequate sunlight.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare a seedbed that supports even emergence and conserve moisture using suitable local practices.
guide.planting: Plant clean seed after effective rainfall and follow extension guidance for spacing, seed rate, and thinning.
guide.nutrition: Use soil tests and local oilseed recommendations. Maintain balanced nutrition without over-applying nitrogen.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Control weeds early and monitor water stress around flowering and seed fill. Maintain drainage after heavy rain.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for head pests, birds, stem or leaf disease, and lodging. Protect pollinators and beneficial insects.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest mature heads when seed is suitably dry, thresh cleanly, and store seed dry to prevent mould and quality loss.
guide.records: Record variety, flowering date, pollinator activity, bird pressure, harvest moisture, and seed quality.

crops.name: Broccoli
crops.summary: A cool-season brassica vegetable. Quality depends on suitable temperature, steady moisture, healthy seedlings, and timely harvest.

guide.siteSelection: Select a cool-season site with reliable water and good drainage. Rotate away from brassicas where clubroot or other soil disease is present.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare a fertile, well-drained seedbed and use healthy transplants.
guide.planting: Choose a locally suitable variety and follow local spacing and transplant-age recommendations.
guide.nutrition: Use soil test results and crop-specific local nutrient guidance. Avoid excessive nitrogen that can affect plant quality.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Maintain even moisture, manage weeds early, and avoid prolonged waterlogging.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for diamondback moth, aphids, caterpillars, downy mildew, and black rot. Use crop rotation, sanitation, netting where appropriate, and official guidance.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest compact heads before flowering, handle gently, shade promptly, and cool or market quickly.
guide.records: Record seedling source, transplant date, irrigation, pest scouting, harvest size, and market quality.

crops.name: Soybeans
crops.summary: A grain and oilseed legume used for food, feed, and processing. Variety maturity, inoculation, and disease history should be checked locally.

guide.siteSelection: Choose a locally adapted variety and a well-drained field; rotate away from recent soybean disease hosts.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare a level, weed-managed seedbed while conserving soil structure and organic matter.
guide.planting: Use clean seed and follow local guidance for planting date, seed rate, spacing, and any recommended inoculant.
guide.nutrition: Use soil tests and local recommendations for pH and nutrient needs; avoid applying inoculants or fertilizers without compatibility guidance.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Manage weeds early and avoid waterlogging; monitor moisture through flowering and pod fill.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for aphids, caterpillars, leaf spots, rust, and pod disease; confirm diagnosis before treatment.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest at suitable maturity, dry thoroughly, clean grain, and protect it from moisture and storage pests.
guide.records: Record variety, seed and inoculant lot, field history, scouting, harvest moisture, and grain quality.

crops.name: Pigeon Peas
crops.summary: A grain and multipurpose legume often grown in mixed systems. Crop duration and market use vary with variety and local conditions.

guide.siteSelection: Choose a suitable local variety and field with drainage; consider the crop's duration and compatibility with intercrops.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare planting stations or rows that support establishment and soil-moisture conservation.
guide.planting: Use healthy seed and follow local advice for spacing, seed rate, planting window, and intercrop arrangement.
guide.nutrition: Use soil-test results and local nutrient recommendations; maintain rotation and organic matter.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Keep young stands weed-managed and conserve moisture; avoid persistent waterlogging.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for pod borers, pod fly, wilt, and leaf spots; remove suspect plants as directed and seek diagnosis.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest when pods mature for the intended green or dry use; dry grain safely and store it clean and pest-protected.
guide.records: Record variety, intercrop, planting dates, pest signs, harvest purpose, and storage.

crops.name: Cowpeas
crops.summary: A food and forage legume grown for leaves, green pods, dry grain, or fodder. Management depends on the selected use and variety.

guide.siteSelection: Select a variety and production purpose suitable for the local rainfall, soil, and market.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare a weed-managed seedbed and use locally suitable rotation or intercropping.
guide.planting: Plant clean seed at the locally recommended time and follow advice for spacing and seed treatment.
guide.nutrition: Use soil tests and local guidance; protect soil organic matter and avoid uncalibrated fertilizer rates.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Control weeds early, maintain drainage, and monitor water stress around flowering and pod fill.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Inspect for aphids, thrips, pod borers, bruchids, and virus-like symptoms; confirm diagnosis before treatment.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest leaves, green pods, or dry grain at the intended stage. Dry grain well and protect it from bruchids and moisture.
guide.records: Record variety, intended use, planting date, scouting, harvest stage, and storage losses.

crops.name: Green Grams
crops.summary: A short-duration grain legume used for food and rotation. Timely planting, weed management, and careful drying support quality.
crops.photoSearch: mung bean green gram crop field

guide.siteSelection: Choose locally suitable seed and a field with good drainage and a suitable rotation history.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare a clean seedbed and conserve soil moisture without leaving the field waterlogged.
guide.planting: Use clean seed and local guidance for planting window, spacing, and seed rate.
guide.nutrition: Use soil-test and extension guidance for nutrient amendments; rotate and retain organic matter where practical.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Control weeds early and monitor moisture through flowering and pod filling.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for aphids, whiteflies, pod borers, bruchids, and leaf disease; seek confirmation for unusual symptoms.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest mature pods in a timely manner, dry thoroughly, and store clean grain in a moisture-protected container.
guide.records: Record seed lot, planting, rainfall, pest observations, harvest rounds, and grain storage condition.

crops.name: Chickpeas
crops.summary: A grain legume best managed with locally tested varieties and disease-aware rotation. Growing suitability is site-specific.

guide.siteSelection: Confirm local suitability and use a well-drained field with a rotation that limits legume disease carry-over.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare a friable seedbed and control volunteer legumes and weeds as advised.
guide.planting: Use clean seed and follow local extension recommendations for season, spacing, seed rate, and treatment.
guide.nutrition: Base pH and nutrient decisions on a soil test and locally calibrated recommendations.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Maintain early weed control and avoid waterlogging; monitor stress during flowering and pod fill.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for pod borers, wilt, and Ascochyta-like lesions; obtain diagnosis before selecting a control.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest mature, dry pods, clean grain, and store in a dry, pest-managed place.
guide.records: Track variety, seed health, field rotation, disease symptoms, harvest date, and storage.

crops.name: Onions
crops.summary: A bulb crop sensitive to weed competition and uneven water. Variety and nursery or direct-seeding method affect crop timing.

guide.siteSelection: Choose a locally suitable variety, well-drained soil, and reliable water; rotate away from recent Allium crops.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare a fine seedbed or raised beds and ensure drainage before transplanting or sowing.
guide.planting: Use healthy seedlings or clean seed and follow local advice for transplant age, spacing, and planting date.
guide.nutrition: Use soil tests and onion-specific local recommendations; avoid excess nitrogen late in bulb development.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Maintain steady moisture without waterlogging and control weeds early, as onions compete poorly when small.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for thrips, downy mildew, purple blotch, and basal rot; remove diseased plants and seek diagnosis.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest when bulbs mature according to local guidance, cure in a dry ventilated place, and store sorted bulbs dry.
guide.records: Record seed lot, nursery dates, transplanting, irrigation, pest scouting, curing, and storage losses.

crops.name: Sweet Potatoes
crops.summary: A root crop grown from vines or cuttings. Clean planting material, soil moisture, and careful harvest help reduce disease and damage.

guide.siteSelection: Select a locally recommended variety and well-drained site with soil suited to root formation.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare ridges or mounds where locally appropriate and remove persistent weeds before planting.
guide.planting: Use healthy, pest-free vine cuttings from a known source and follow local guidance on spacing and planting window.
guide.nutrition: Use soil-test and local extension advice; avoid excessive nitrogen that can favor vine growth over roots.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Keep the crop weed-free during establishment and maintain moisture while avoiding waterlogging.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for sweet potato weevils, virus-like leaf symptoms, and rots; avoid moving infected vines between farms.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Lift roots carefully at maturity, cure and sort as locally advised, and protect from cuts, heat, and moisture.
guide.records: Record variety, vine source, planting date, pest observations, harvest size, and storage or marketing losses.

crops.name: Cassava
crops.summary: A staple root crop propagated by stem cuttings. Planting-material health and safe post-harvest processing are essential.

guide.siteSelection: Choose a locally suitable variety and a field with drainage; consider the planned harvest age and market.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare planting stations or ridges as locally advised and conserve soil on sloping land.
guide.planting: Use healthy cuttings from known, disease-managed sources and follow local guidance on cutting size and spacing.
guide.nutrition: Use soil tests and local recommendations; maintain rotation and organic matter rather than relying on repeated nutrient removal.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Control weeds during establishment and keep drainage functional. Monitor drought stress in young plants.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Inspect for cassava mosaic and brown streak-like symptoms, mealybugs, and mites; do not distribute suspect cuttings.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest roots carefully when suited to the variety and market. Process promptly using established safe methods; fresh roots do not store long.
guide.records: Record variety, cutting source, planting dates, disease signs, harvest age, and processing or sales.

crops.name: Cabbage
crops.summary: A brassica vegetable grown from seedlings or direct seed. Rotation and regular scouting help manage caterpillars and leaf diseases.

guide.siteSelection: Choose a locally suitable variety, reliable water, and a field rotated away from brassicas.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare a fertile, well-drained bed and use healthy seedlings from a trusted source.
guide.planting: Follow local guidance for nursery, transplant age, spacing, and planting season.
guide.nutrition: Use soil-test results and locally recommended brassica nutrition; avoid blanket fertilizer rates.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Maintain consistent moisture, control weeds early, and avoid waterlogging.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for diamondback moth, aphids, caterpillars, black rot, and clubroot; confirm symptoms before treatment.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest firm heads at market maturity, handle gently, shade promptly, and remove damaged leaves.
guide.records: Record seed source, transplant date, pest scouting, crop protection decisions, harvest grade, and losses.

crops.name: Kale
crops.summary: A leafy brassica harvested over multiple pickings. Regular leaf inspection and clean harvest practices support quality.

guide.siteSelection: Select a suitable variety and a well-drained site with dependable water; rotate away from brassicas where feasible.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare a fine seedbed or transplant bed and remove weeds before establishment.
guide.planting: Use healthy seed or seedlings and follow local spacing and harvest-system advice.
guide.nutrition: Base nutrient additions on soil tests and locally recommended leafy-crop guidance.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Maintain even moisture, manage weeds early, and avoid prolonged wet foliage where possible.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Inspect leaf undersides for aphids and caterpillars and scout for leaf spots and downy mildew; confirm unusual signs.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest leaves cleanly and repeatedly without damaging the growing point; keep produce shaded and cool.
guide.records: Record variety, planting, harvest rounds, pest observations, market grade, and post-harvest handling.

crops.name: Spinach
crops.summary: A leafy vegetable requiring clean water, fertile soil, and gentle handling. Locally grown amaranths and other greens are different crops.

guide.siteSelection: Choose a cool-enough local planting window, well-drained bed, and clean irrigation source.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare a fine seedbed with good drainage and remove weeds before sowing.
guide.planting: Use fresh, quality seed and follow local recommendations for spacing and successive sowing.
guide.nutrition: Use soil-test guidance and safe, well-managed organic amendments; avoid fresh manure near harvest.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Keep moisture even, avoid waterlogging, and control weeds without contaminating leaves.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for leaf miners, aphids, leaf spots, and downy mildew; remove badly affected material and confirm diagnosis.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest clean leaves at the desired size, avoid soil contamination, shade promptly, and market quickly.
guide.records: Record seed lot, sowing dates, water source, harvest rounds, hygiene checks, and rejected produce.

crops.name: Carrots
crops.summary: A root crop that benefits from a fine, stone-free seedbed and even moisture during root formation.

guide.siteSelection: Choose a deep, loose, well-drained site and a variety suitable for local soil and market needs.
guide.landPreparation: Remove stones and clods and prepare a fine seedbed; compact or shallow soil can distort roots.
guide.planting: Sow clean seed at the locally advised spacing and thin carefully if required.
guide.nutrition: Use soil tests and local recommendations; avoid excessive fresh manure or nitrogen that can impair root quality.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Maintain even moisture during germination and root expansion and control weeds early.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for leaf diseases, nematode damage, and root rots; use rotation and confirm the cause of poor roots.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Lift roots carefully at market size, remove excess soil without injury, and store cool and humid as locally advised.
guide.records: Record variety, seed date, thinning, irrigation, root grading, and storage losses.

crops.name: Sweet Peppers
crops.summary: A fruiting vegetable that needs healthy seedlings, steady moisture, and scouting for sap-feeding pests and fruit disease.
crops.photoSearch: sweet pepper bell pepper crop field

guide.siteSelection: Select a locally suitable variety and a well-drained field rotated away from other solanaceous crops.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare beds with drainage and use healthy, hardened seedlings.
guide.planting: Transplant at the locally recommended age and spacing; provide support where the variety or system needs it.
guide.nutrition: Use soil tests and crop-stage recommendations; avoid unbalanced inputs and fertilizer contact with roots.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Maintain regular moisture without waterlogging, mulch where suitable, and control weeds early.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for thrips, aphids, whiteflies, bacterial spots, and fruit rots; remove suspect plants and seek diagnosis.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest fruit at the required color and maturity, handle gently, shade, and sort damaged produce.
guide.records: Record variety, transplant date, irrigation, pest scouting, market maturity, and harvest grade.

crops.name: Avocados
crops.summary: A perennial fruit crop. Variety, rootstock, pollination, drainage, and buyer maturity standards should be matched to the production area.

guide.siteSelection: Choose suitable varieties for the local climate and market, with deep drainage and protection from damaging winds.
guide.landPreparation: Plan orchard spacing, access, drainage, and erosion control before planting.
guide.planting: Use healthy, true-to-type planting material from a reliable source and follow local orchard-establishment advice.
guide.nutrition: Use soil and leaf analysis where available; base nutrient and lime decisions on orchard age and local recommendations.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Protect young trees from moisture stress while preventing waterlogging; keep mulch away from trunks and manage orchard cover.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for root rots, fruit flies, borers, and leaf or fruit diseases; use sanitation and get a confirmed diagnosis.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest at maturity standards set for the variety and buyer, avoid fruit injury, and handle and transport in shade.
guide.records: Track variety, tree age, flowering, orchard inputs, pest observations, harvest maturity, and buyer quality feedback.

crops.name: Mangoes
crops.summary: A perennial fruit crop with variety-specific flowering, harvest, and market requirements. Orchard hygiene helps reduce pest and disease pressure.

guide.siteSelection: Select variety and planting material suited to local rainfall, soil drainage, orchard spacing, and intended market.
guide.landPreparation: Plan drainage, access, wind protection, and erosion control before establishing trees.
guide.planting: Use healthy grafted or otherwise locally recommended planting material and extension guidance for establishment and pruning.
guide.nutrition: Use soil-test guidance and recommendations that consider tree age, flowering, and harvest; avoid generic rates.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Maintain young-tree moisture, protect the root zone, and manage ground cover without damaging roots.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for fruit flies, powdery mildew, anthracnose, and scale insects; remove fallen fruit and seek local diagnosis.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest at variety- and buyer-appropriate maturity, prevent latex and bruising damage, and keep fruit shaded.
guide.records: Record variety, tree age, flowering, pest monitoring, harvest grade, and post-harvest losses.

crops.name: Citrus
crops.summary: A group of perennial fruit crops. Species, rootstock, local disease status, and market maturity affect orchard choices.

guide.siteSelection: Identify the citrus species and choose locally recommended planting material and a well-drained site.
guide.landPreparation: Plan orchard layout, drainage, access, and wind protection before planting.
guide.planting: Use healthy certified or otherwise trusted nursery stock and follow local guidance for spacing and pruning.
guide.nutrition: Use soil tests and citrus-specific recommendations; do not copy rates from another orchard or crop.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Manage irrigation and orchard floor cover to protect roots and prevent waterlogging.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Inspect leaves, branches, and fruit for citrus canker-like lesions, greening-like symptoms, scale, and fruit flies; report suspected regulated disease.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest by variety and buyer maturity standards, avoid fruit injury, and store and transport in clean shaded conditions.
guide.records: Record species, nursery source, tree age, disease scouting, harvest timing, and fruit grade.

crops.name: Sesame
crops.summary: An oilseed crop with small seed and maturity-sensitive harvest. Variety and planting time should fit local rainfall and buyer requirements.

guide.siteSelection: Choose a locally adapted variety and well-drained field with a suitable rotation history.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare a fine seedbed for uniform emergence while conserving soil moisture.
guide.planting: Use quality seed and local advice on planting time, seed rate, spacing, and thinning.
guide.nutrition: Use soil tests and locally calibrated oilseed recommendations; avoid untested fertilizer rates.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Control weeds early and maintain drainage; monitor moisture during establishment and flowering.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for capsule feeders, leaf spots, and wilt; confirm signs and seek local advice before treatment.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest at the locally recommended maturity to limit shattering, dry bundles or seed safely, and store clean and dry.
guide.records: Record variety, seed source, planting window, pest signs, harvest timing, and seed cleanliness.

crops.name: Castor
crops.summary: An oilseed crop with important handling and toxicity considerations. Keep castor seed and plant parts away from children and livestock.

guide.siteSelection: Confirm commercial suitability, locally approved variety, and buyer arrangements before production.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare a well-drained planting site and plan safe access and separation from food or feed handling areas.
guide.planting: Use reliable seed and follow local guidance for planting window, spacing, and crop establishment.
guide.nutrition: Use soil tests and crop-specific local recommendations.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Manage weeds during establishment and maintain drainage; monitor moisture without over-irrigating.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for capsule pests, leaf spots, and wilt; obtain diagnosis and follow official crop-protection guidance.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Use protective handling, keep seed contained, and store securely away from children, food, and livestock feed.
guide.records: Record seed source, field location, worker safety procedures, harvest lots, and secure storage.

crops.name: Sugarcane
crops.summary: A long-duration crop usually linked to a mill or local processing market. Variety, planting material, water, and delivery arrangements are essential.

guide.siteSelection: Confirm local suitability, water availability, soil drainage, mill or buyer terms, and transport before planting.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare rows and drainage according to the production system and conserve soil on slopes.
guide.planting: Use clean, recommended setts or planting material and follow local guidance for row layout and planting season.
guide.nutrition: Use soil testing and local cane recommendations; coordinate nutrient timing with crop stage and water access.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Manage irrigation and drainage as advised locally and keep the field weed-managed during establishment.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for borers, smut, mosaic symptoms, and stalk rots; use clean planting material and report unusual disease.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest and deliver according to mill or buyer schedules; minimize delay and contamination after cutting.
guide.records: Track variety, sett source, ratoon number, input use, harvest weight, delivery time, and buyer deductions.

crops.name: Tobacco
crops.summary: A regulated contract and market crop in many areas. Follow current government, buyer, worker-safety, and environmental requirements.

guide.siteSelection: Confirm current local regulations, buyer contract, variety, rotation, and curing facilities before planting.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare nursery and field sites with drainage and soil conservation suited to local guidance.
guide.planting: Use approved seed and healthy seedlings and follow the buyer and extension service's current schedule and spacing advice.
guide.nutrition: Use soil tests and crop-specific official recommendations; avoid excess inputs and protect water sources.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Manage moisture and weeds with locally approved practices; avoid contamination of nearby crops and water.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for caterpillars, aphids, wilt, and leaf disease; use only registered products and follow all safety requirements.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest and cure according to the contracted system, maintain ventilation and fire safety, and protect cured leaf from moisture.
guide.records: Keep contract, seed, input, worker safety, pesticide label, curing, and sales records.

crops.name: Sisal
crops.summary: A perennial fibre crop whose establishment and leaf processing are location- and market-specific. Worker safety during cutting and processing matters.

guide.siteSelection: Confirm suitability, planting material, land tenure, processing access, and buyer arrangements with local extension services.
guide.landPreparation: Plan rows, access paths, drainage, and erosion control for the plantation lifespan.
guide.planting: Use healthy planting material and locally advised spacing and establishment methods.
guide.nutrition: Use local soil and crop guidance; avoid fertilizer decisions based solely on another plantation.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Control weeds around young plants and maintain field access and drainage.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Inspect plants for rot, leaf damage, and unusual decline; report suspected disease and use clean planting material.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Harvest leaves at locally advised maturity and process with safe equipment and protective practices.
guide.records: Record planting source, block and plant age, harvest cycles, worker safety, processing, and fibre quality.

crops.name: Pyrethrum
crops.summary: A flowering crop grown for pyrethrin-containing flowers. Variety, harvest standard, processing, and buyer requirements are locally specific.

guide.siteSelection: Confirm elevation, climate, variety, buyer requirements, and suitability with local pyrethrum extension services.
guide.landPreparation: Prepare a weed-managed, well-drained site and plan field access for repeated flower picking.
guide.planting: Use recommended seed or seedlings from a reliable source and follow local guidance for nursery, spacing, and planting date.
guide.nutrition: Use soil-test results and pyrethrum-specific local recommendations; do not copy fertilizer rates from other crops.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Manage weeds during establishment and maintain suitable moisture and drainage for the local production system.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Scout for flower, leaf, and root disease or pest damage and seek diagnosis before selecting control measures.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Pick flowers at the buyer- and extension-recommended stage, dry and handle them safely, and protect dried material from moisture and contamination.
guide.records: Record seed source, planting, flower-picking rounds, dry-flower quality, processing, and buyer feedback.

crops.name: Timber trees
crops.scientificName: Species varies by tree and production system
crops.summary: Timber is a group of tree species rather than one crop. Species suitability, permits, rotation, and harvest rules must be verified locally.

guide.siteSelection: Identify the tree species and confirm land suitability, water needs, fire risk, and current forestry requirements.
guide.landPreparation: Plan spacing, access, firebreaks, soil protection, and compatible crops or grazing before establishment.
guide.planting: Use healthy seedlings from a reliable nursery and follow forestry advice for planting season and spacing.
guide.nutrition: Base soil amendments on tests and species-specific forestry recommendations.
guide.waterAndWeeds: Protect seedlings from competition and drought; maintain safe firebreaks and avoid damage to neighboring habitats.
guide.pestsAndDiseases: Monitor seedlings and stands for dieback, borers, and leaf disease; seek forestry-extension diagnosis.
guide.harvestAndStorage: Confirm permits and sustainable harvest rules before cutting. Store and transport logs safely and according to legal requirements.
guide.records: Record species, seedling source, planting date, block map, survival, thinning, permits, and harvest.

livestock.name: Cattle
livestock.summary: Keep separate plans for dairy, beef, draught, and breeding animals; body condition, water, forage availability, and disease risk vary by production system.

care.feed: Base the diet on safe forage or grazing, clean water, and a balanced supplement appropriate to age, pregnancy, lactation, and body condition. Introduce feed changes gradually; ask a livestock officer to formulate rations.
care.housing: Provide shade, ventilation, dry resting areas, drainage, secure fencing, and enough space for animals to stand and lie. Clean water and feed troughs regularly.
care.health: Maintain a relationship with a registered veterinarian or livestock extension officer. Follow official vaccination and parasite-control schedules for the district; isolate sick or newly introduced animals and record treatments and withdrawal periods.
care.breeding: Record animal ID, service or bull exposure, pregnancy checks, calving, and calf outcomes. Seek timely assistance for difficult birth or retained placenta.
care.warningSigns: Urgently seek veterinary help for inability to stand, breathing difficulty, severe bloat, bloody diarrhea, sudden milk drop with fever, abortion clusters, or unexplained deaths.
care.dailyRecords: Record ID/tag, feed and water, health signs, treatments, milk or weight, breeding dates, calving, movement, and sales.

livestock.name: Goats
livestock.summary: Adaptable browsers and grazers. Browse access, clean housing, parasite monitoring, and kid survival are key management areas.

care.feed: Provide safe browse or forage, clean water, and a mineral supplement suited to local advice. Pregnant, lactating, growing, and breeding goats have different needs; avoid sudden diet changes and mouldy feed.
care.housing: Use dry, well-ventilated shelter with raised or well-drained resting areas, secure fencing, and space to separate kids, new arrivals, and sick animals.
care.health: Follow district vaccination and parasite guidance. Inspect feet, coat, eyelids, appetite, and feces; quarantine new arrivals and seek advice before deworming.
care.breeding: Record buck access, mating dates, pregnancy checks, kidding, litter size, and kid survival. Provide supervision and clean dry areas around kidding.
care.warningSigns: Seek veterinary help for sudden weakness, severe diarrhea, respiratory distress, neurological signs, swollen jaw, abortion clusters, or rapid deaths.
care.dailyRecords: Track tag, age, body condition, feed, parasite signs, treatment, mating, kidding, kid growth, and sales.

livestock.name: Sheep
livestock.summary: Flock management needs vary by meat, wool, and breeding purpose. Parasite control, foot care, lambing preparation, and clean forage matter.

care.feed: Provide good-quality forage or grazing, clean water, and supplements based on growth, pregnancy, lactation, and body condition. Use only locally appropriate mineral mixes.
care.housing: Keep shelter dry and ventilated with secure fencing, clean bedding, adequate space, and separate pens for lambing, quarantine, and sick animals.
care.health: Follow local vaccination and parasite advice. Monitor feet, fleece/coat, appetite, body condition, and lamb growth; have treatments prescribed or confirmed by a qualified animal-health worker.
care.breeding: Record ram joining dates, lambing, litter size, lamb identification, and survival. Prepare a clean, quiet lambing area.
care.warningSigns: Seek veterinary help for sudden death, severe lameness, bloat, breathing difficulty, neurological signs, abortion clusters, or lambs unable to suck.
care.dailyRecords: Record flock IDs, feed, body condition, parasite signs, treatments, mating, lambing, growth, and sales.

livestock.name: Chickens
livestock.summary: For broilers, layers, and indigenous birds, use a plan suited to breed, production stage, housing, and local disease risk.

care.feed: Use a complete feed appropriate to chick, grower, layer, or broiler stage. Provide clean water continuously; store feed dry and protected from rodents and mould. Do not use unbalanced scraps as the sole ration.
care.housing: Provide dry litter, ventilation without chilling drafts, predator protection, suitable stocking density, clean drinkers, and a brooding area with age-appropriate warmth.
care.health: Obtain a vaccination schedule from a veterinarian or livestock extension office. Keep a closed-flock or controlled-entry approach, quarantine arrivals, clean equipment, and report sudden mortality.
care.breeding: For breeding flocks, record parent groups, egg collection, fertility, incubation, hatch, and chick losses. Keep hatchery hygiene and egg handling controlled.
care.warningSigns: Seek urgent advice for sudden deaths, gasping, twisted necks, green or bloody diarrhea, sharp drops in feed/water intake, or a rapid egg-production decline.
care.dailyRecords: Record flock age, number alive, feed and water, egg count, vaccination, mortality, symptoms, and treatments.

livestock.name: Ducks
livestock.summary: Ducks can be raised for eggs or meat; access to clean drinking water and dry resting areas is more important than a pond.

care.feed: Use balanced waterfowl feed suitable for age and purpose with uninterrupted clean drinking water. Prevent feed from becoming wet, mouldy, or contaminated.
care.housing: Provide a dry, ventilated, predator-proof house, absorbent bedding, safe outdoor area, and water containers designed to limit wet litter.
care.health: Use veterinary guidance for vaccination and disease prevention; quarantine new birds, clean equipment, and avoid mixing unknown flocks.
care.breeding: Track breeding groups, egg collection, incubation, hatch, and duckling survival. Use clean nesting and incubation practices.
care.warningSigns: Seek help for sudden deaths, inability to walk, breathing problems, neurological signs, or rapid declines in eating, drinking, or laying.
care.dailyRecords: Record age, flock count, feed and water, egg count, hatch, mortality, and any treatment.

livestock.name: Turkeys
livestock.summary: Turkeys require careful brooding and biosecurity and should not automatically share housing or equipment with other poultry.

care.feed: Provide complete feed formulated for turkey growth stage. Ensure easy access to clean water and avoid feeding mouldy grain or an unbalanced diet.
care.housing: Keep brooding conditions stable, litter dry, ventilation adequate, and predators excluded. Separate age groups and avoid mixed-species housing when disease risk is unclear.
care.health: Ask a veterinarian about local vaccination and parasite plans. Clean and disinfect housing between flocks; isolate new or sick birds.
care.breeding: Keep parent-bird, egg, hatch, and poult records. Handle eggs and young poults carefully and maintain clean incubation equipment.
care.warningSigns: Seek advice for sudden mortality, poor coordination, respiratory signs, severe diarrhea, or poor growth across a group.
care.dailyRecords: Record flock age and count, feed, water, mortality, vaccination, egg/hatch results, and treatments.

livestock.name: Quail
livestock.scientificName: Coturnix japonica and related domestic quail
livestock.summary: Small poultry requiring fine feed, secure housing, and careful temperature and hygiene management.

care.feed: Use a nutritionally complete feed designed for quail and life stage; particles must be suitable for small birds. Provide clean water and prevent feed spoilage.
care.housing: Use secure, well-ventilated housing with appropriate floor or cage design, protection from drafts and predators, and regular manure and litter management.
care.health: Source chicks or eggs responsibly, quarantine new stock, and obtain a local veterinary health plan. Clean drinkers and equipment consistently.
care.breeding: Track breeder groups, egg production, fertility, incubation, hatch, and chick losses; keep incubators clean and stable.
care.warningSigns: Seek help for sudden deaths, weakness, breathing signs, diarrhea, or rapid changes in egg production.
care.dailyRecords: Track bird numbers, feed and water, egg counts, mortality, hatch performance, and any health actions.

livestock.name: Pigs
livestock.summary: Pig production depends on balanced feed, dry comfortable housing, clean water, and strict prevention of African swine fever spread.

care.feed: Use balanced pig feed matched to piglets, growers, finishers, or sows. Never feed unsafe swill containing animal products unless specifically permitted and properly treated under current government rules.
care.housing: Provide shade, ventilation, dry lying space, secure fencing, drainage, and reliable clean water. Separate age groups and provide safe farrowing pens.
care.health: Restrict visitors and animal movement, clean and disinfect equipment, quarantine arrivals, and contact authorities promptly for suspected African swine fever. Do not move or sell sick pigs.
care.breeding: Record boar or insemination dates, pregnancy checks, farrowing, litter size, piglet identification, and weaning.
care.warningSigns: Urgently report sudden deaths, high fever, red or purple skin, bleeding, abortion clusters, or rapid illness in several pigs.
care.dailyRecords: Track IDs, feed, water, weight, mating, farrowing, mortality, movement, cleaning, and sales.

livestock.name: Rabbits
livestock.summary: Rabbits are sensitive to heat, sudden diet changes, and dirty housing; steady forage and clean water are essential.

care.feed: Provide clean forage or hay and a balanced rabbit ration as locally recommended. Introduce greens gradually, provide clean water, and avoid mouldy feed.
care.housing: Keep housing cool, shaded, dry, ventilated, secure from predators, and easy to clean. Provide adequate space and suitable nesting boxes for kindling.
care.health: Quarantine new rabbits, maintain hygiene, and obtain veterinary advice for local vaccination or parasite risks. Monitor teeth, feet, droppings, and appetite.
care.breeding: Record mating, kindling, litter size, kit survival, and weaning. Avoid repeated breeding that compromises doe condition.
care.warningSigns: Seek advice promptly for not eating, no droppings, severe diarrhea, breathing difficulty, head tilt, or sudden deaths.
care.dailyRecords: Record animal ID, feed, water, body condition, mating, kindling, kit growth, and health observations.

livestock.name: Farmed fish
livestock.summary: Pond and tank management is species- and water-system-specific. Water quality and stocking decisions need local fisheries guidance.

care.feed: Use species- and life-stage-appropriate aquaculture feed and a measured feeding plan. Remove excess feed and store feed dry; avoid polluting the water.
care.housing: Maintain pond, cage, or tank integrity, safe water exchange, appropriate stocking, and escape prevention. Do not transfer fish or water between sites without biosecurity advice.
care.health: Observe feeding, swimming, gills, skin, and mortality. Contact fisheries officers or aquatic animal-health specialists for unusual disease or deaths; do not use unapproved medicines.
care.breeding: Record species, broodstock source, spawning, fry batches, grading, and transfers. Follow local hatchery and movement rules.
care.warningSigns: Investigate rapid mortality, gasping at the surface, erratic swimming, lesions, or a sudden stop in feeding; check water quality and seek expert help.
care.dailyRecords: Record water observations, feed quantity, stock counts, mortality, treatments, growth sampling, and harvest.

livestock.name: Bee colonies
livestock.scientificName: Apis mellifera and locally kept bee species
livestock.summary: Beekeeping requires safe hive placement, responsible handling, forage awareness, and protection from pesticide exposure.

care.feed: Maintain forage access across seasons. Supplement only when a trained beekeeper recommends it and use clean equipment; avoid contaminating honey supers.
care.housing: Site hives away from public paths and livestock, secure them from fire and theft, and maintain safe inspection access and protective clothing.
care.health: Inspect colonies using suitable protective gear and local guidance. Avoid moving colonies or using treatments without a trained beekeeper or extension recommendation.
care.breeding: Record colony origin, queen status, swarming, splits, and replacement. Follow local rules for colony movement.
care.warningSigns: Seek trained help for sudden colony loss, abnormal brood patterns, heavy pest infestation, or suspected pesticide poisoning. Report suspected poisoning through official channels.
care.dailyRecords: Record hive ID and location, inspections, colony strength, queen observations, forage, treatments, honey harvest, and movement.

livestock.name: Donkeys
livestock.summary: Working equids need appropriate forage, clean water, rest, humane handling, and routine hoof and dental care.

care.feed: Provide adequate forage, clean water, and a balanced supplement only where needed. Feed changes should be gradual; avoid mouldy or contaminated feed.
care.housing: Provide shade, dry shelter, secure fencing, clean bedding, and safe turnout. Do not tether in a way that risks injury or prevents access to water.
care.health: Arrange routine veterinary checks, hoof care, dental assessment, and parasite advice. Clean equipment and avoid overloading or working an ill animal.
care.breeding: Record jenny and jack identity, mating, pregnancy, foaling, and foal outcomes; seek veterinary support for difficult birth.
care.warningSigns: Urgently seek help for colic signs, inability to bear weight, wounds, breathing distress, not eating, or sudden weakness.
care.dailyRecords: Record animal ID, body condition, work and rest, feed and water, hoof care, illness, treatment, and movement.

livestock.name: Camels
livestock.summary: Camel care varies by species, local environment, and production purpose. Use local veterinary and livestock-extension guidance.

care.feed: Provide locally available safe browse or forage and dependable clean water. Adjust feed to age, pregnancy, lactation, work, and body condition.
care.housing: Provide shade, secure handling facilities, safe fencing, and dry resting areas; avoid crowding and allow appropriate movement.
care.health: Use a veterinarian familiar with camels for routine health, vaccination, parasite, and movement advice. Quarantine new animals and record treatments.
care.breeding: Record animal identity, mating dates, pregnancy checks, calving, and calf growth. Seek experienced help for handling and difficult births.
care.warningSigns: Seek veterinary help for inability to stand, severe dehydration, breathing difficulty, wounds, sudden loss of appetite, or unexplained deaths.
care.dailyRecords: Record ID, body condition, feed and water, work, health observations, treatment, breeding, and movement.

livestock.name: Other farm animals
livestock.summary: Use this guide as a safety checklist for species not listed elsewhere; obtain species-specific husbandry advice before keeping or treating animals.

care.feed: Identify the species and life stage before feeding. Use a nutritionally suitable diet and clean water; avoid unfamiliar or mouldy feed.
care.housing: Provide species-appropriate space, shelter, ventilation, fencing, and protection from predators and extreme weather.
care.health: Ask a qualified veterinarian or livestock officer for species-specific vaccination, parasite, quarantine, and treatment guidance.
care.breeding: Keep individual identification and breeding records and seek qualified advice before breeding unfamiliar species.
care.warningSigns: Isolate animals with severe or rapidly worsening signs and contact an animal-health professional; report unusual deaths or suspected notifiable disease.
care.dailyRecords: Record species, source, ID, feed, water, health observations, treatment, movement, and any production.

threats.name: Fall armyworm
threats.symptoms: Young larvae can cause window-pane scraping; larger larvae may leave ragged leaves and frass in the whorl. Similar damage can have other causes.
threats.prevention: Scout early and repeatedly, conserve natural enemies, remove volunteer host plants where advised, and use locally appropriate planting and crop sanitation practices.
threats.response: Check several plants across the field and record affected area and crop stage. Ask extension staff to confirm the pest. Use only current TPHPA-registered products when necessary and follow the specific label.
threats.urgent: Escalate widespread damage, uncertain identification, or rapidly worsening infestations to the local agricultural extension officer.

threats.name: Tomato leafminer
threats.symptoms: Larvae make irregular mines in leaves and can damage shoots and fruit. Confirm the insect; other leafminers can look similar.
threats.prevention: Use healthy seedlings, monitor plants frequently, remove infested residues safely, rotate crops, and clean tools and containers.
threats.response: Use scouting and suitable traps only as advised locally. Seek extension diagnosis and check current TPHPA registration and label before considering crop protection products.
threats.urgent: Escalate rapidly spreading damage or suspected resistance to extension staff.

threats.name: Maize stalk borers
threats.symptoms: Shot holes, frass, tunnelling in stems, broken plants, or dead-heart symptoms can occur. Several borers and stresses may produce similar signs.
threats.prevention: Use locally recommended varieties and planting practices, scout young crops, manage crop residues using extension advice, and rotate where suitable.
threats.response: Split stems of affected plants to inspect for larvae and tunnels; report crop stage and affected area. Ask extension staff about locally suitable cultural or biological controls.
threats.urgent: Seek advice when damage spreads quickly or the crop is near a sensitive growth stage.

threats.name: Bean rust
threats.symptoms: Small orange-brown pustules may appear, often on leaf undersides. Confirm carefully; nutrient injury and other leaf diseases can be confused with rust.
threats.prevention: Use clean seed and resistant varieties when locally available, rotate crops, manage volunteers, and avoid prolonged leaf wetness where possible.
threats.response: Record the field and affected plants and seek a diagnosis before treatment. Follow TPHPA guidance and product labels if a registered treatment is recommended.
threats.urgent: Escalate disease appearing early or spreading across multiple fields.

threats.name: Maize lethal necrosis (suspected)
threats.scientificName: Maize chlorotic mottle virus with a potyvirus
threats.symptoms: Chlorosis, mottling, leaf necrosis, stunting, and poor or absent ears may be seen. Visual symptoms alone are not confirmation.
threats.prevention: Use clean seed, control volunteer maize as advised, monitor vectors and crop hygiene, and use varieties and practices recommended by official local guidance.
threats.response: Do not move suspect plants or seed. Photograph symptoms, note field location and crop stage, and contact an extension officer or plant-health authority for confirmation.
threats.urgent: Report suspected outbreaks promptly to local plant-health authorities.

threats.name: Late blight
threats.symptoms: Water-soaked lesions that enlarge and darken can appear on leaves and stems; under humid conditions growth may appear at lesion edges. Confirmation is important.
threats.prevention: Use healthy planting material, rotate crops, remove infected volunteers as advised, improve airflow, and avoid unnecessary leaf wetness.
threats.response: Seek fast local diagnosis when disease spreads under wet conditions. Use registered products only when an extension officer recommends them and follow the label and pre-harvest interval.
threats.urgent: Escalate immediately when lesions spread rapidly in cool, wet weather.

threats.name: Coffee leaf rust
threats.symptoms: Yellowish spots on leaf upper surfaces and orange powdery pustules below may occur, with leaf loss in severe cases.
threats.prevention: Maintain appropriate shade and pruning for the local system, use recommended varieties, and monitor during conducive weather.
threats.response: Ask coffee extension staff to confirm the disease and assess severity. Follow current local TPHPA-approved recommendations.
threats.urgent: Seek advice for defoliation or spread across neighboring coffee plots.

threats.name: Peste des petits ruminants (PPR) — suspected
threats.symptoms: Fever, eye or nose discharge, mouth lesions, breathing difficulty, diarrhea, and sudden illness in several small ruminants can be warning signs; other diseases can look similar.
threats.prevention: Follow official vaccination campaigns, quarantine arrivals, limit mixing and movement, and disinfect shared equipment.
threats.response: Isolate affected animals and contact a veterinarian or district livestock officer immediately. Do not move or sell sick animals.
threats.urgent: Treat suspected PPR as urgent and report it to animal-health authorities.

threats.name: Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) — suspected
threats.photoSearch: cattle foot and mouth disease lesions
threats.symptoms: Fever, excessive salivation, mouth blisters or sores, and lameness may occur. Clinical signs require official veterinary confirmation.
threats.prevention: Follow current government movement controls and vaccination advice. Maintain farm entry hygiene and avoid contact with neighboring herds during an alert.
threats.response: Immediately restrict animal movement and contact district veterinary authorities. Do not transport, sell, or slaughter affected animals unless directed by officials.
threats.urgent: Report suspected FMD immediately; movement restrictions may apply.

threats.name: Newcastle disease — suspected
threats.symptoms: Respiratory, digestive, or nervous signs and sudden flock deaths may occur. Signs vary and cannot confirm the disease on their own.
threats.prevention: Follow a veterinarian-approved vaccination schedule, keep poultry housing and equipment clean, control visitors, and separate age groups.
threats.response: Isolate the flock, stop bird movement, and contact veterinary or district livestock services. Do not sell or give away sick or dead birds.
threats.urgent: Report sudden or unusual poultry deaths to local animal-health authorities.

threats.name: African swine fever (ASF) — suspected
threats.symptoms: Sudden high fever, weakness, skin discoloration, bleeding, abortions, or deaths can be warning signs. Laboratory and official veterinary assessment is required.
threats.prevention: Use strict visitor and equipment biosecurity, quarantine new pigs, avoid unsafe swill feeding, and follow current government rules on movement and disinfection.
threats.response: Stop movement of pigs and products, isolate the premises, and notify animal-health authorities immediately. Do not slaughter, sell, or dispose of carcasses without official instructions.
threats.urgent: ASF is notifiable in many jurisdictions; report suspicion immediately and follow Tanzania authority instructions.
